plan.title: Mouse liver HFD vs chow: DE genes and hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: Design: 6 high-fat-diet vs 6 chow mouse liver samples, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon-derived gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples). One caveat: sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median. Per the sourced RNA-seq DE procedure, we do not drop this sample by default — DESeq2's size-factor normalization accounts for depth, and removal is a judgment call, not a default response to low depth. The plan therefore runs (1) a sample-structure QC step that computes library sizes, a blind-VST PCA, and a sample-distance heatmap specifically to characterize sample_01 (does it cluster with its condition group or is it an outlier on more than depth?) and issues a data-driven keep/exclude recommendation with a stated reason; (2) DESeq2 differential expression (minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization, explicit reference level = chow/control, Wald test, apeglm LFC shrinkage, BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05); (3) fgsea preranked GSEA against the MSigDB mouse Hallmark collection (2026.1, staged locally) using the DESeq2 Wald statistic as the ranking metric, respecting the 15-500 gene set size window and reporting leading-edge genes; (4) an integrated report presenting DE gene tables (shrunken and unshrunken LFC), fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), the hallmark pathway results, and full reproducibility metadata (versions, seed, collection version). The QC step's finding about sample_01 is treated as gating information for step 2, not pre-decided.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) PCA + sample distance heatmap + library size QC
Minimal pre-filter: >=10 counts in >=6 samples (smallest group size)
DESeq2 design ~condition, explicit reference level = chow/control
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic vs MSigDB mouse Hallmark
Integrated DE + pathway report with QC, diagnostics, leading edge, reproducibility record
